CheckTitle: Privileged application registrations should not have federated identity credentials
Description: Microsoft Entra **application registrations** that hold a **Control Plane (Tier 0) directory role** should not also have **federated identity credentials**. Such a credential grants an external issuer/subject pair standing token exchange to the application with no stored secret and no expiry, letting an external workload act with the application's privileged rights.
Risk: A **federated identity credential** lets an external issuer/subject pair (a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI job, for example) mint tokens for the application with no stored secret and no expiry. When the application's service principal also holds a **Tier 0 (Control Plane) directory role**, that external workload can act with tenant-takeover privileges from the external provider's namespace.

Code.Other:
1. Navigate to Microsoft Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com)
2. Go to Applications > App registrations
3. Select the flagged application
4. Review whether the application needs its Control Plane (Tier 0) directory role; if not, remove the role assignment under Roles and administrators
5. If the role is required, go to Certificates & secrets > Federated credentials and confirm each credential's issuer and subject are tightly scoped to a specific external identity, removing any that are unnecessary
6. Prefer isolating privileged automation into a dedicated application with a narrowly scoped federated credential

Recommendation.Text: Do not combine federated identity credentials with Control Plane (Tier 0) directory roles on the same application. Either scope the application down so it no longer holds a privileged role, or move the privileged workload to a dedicated application whose federated credential subject and issuer are tightly restricted to the intended external identity.

Notes: Federated identity credentials are the recommended replacement for client secrets, so their mere presence is not flagged. This check only reports the highest-signal case: a federated identity credential on an application whose service principal holds a permanent Tier 0 (Control Plane) directory role. Privileged status is modeled the same way as entra_service_principal_no_secrets_for_permanent_tier0_roles.
